sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ubhau dharmau mahābhāgāv ubhau paramaduścarau ubhau mahāphalau tāta sadbhir ācaritāv ubhau
english: Bhīṣma said: Both ways of duty, my son, are exalted, both exceedingly hard to tread, both bear great fruit, and both have been practised by the good.

sanskrit: atra te vartayiṣyāmi prāmāṇyam ubhayos tayoḥ śṛṇuṣvaikamanāḥ pārtha chinnadharmārthasaṃśayam
english: On this I shall set forth for you the authority of them both. Listen with single-minded attention, Pārtha, and your doubts about duty and its purpose will be cut away.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam kapilasya goś ca saṃvādaṃ tan nibodha yudhiṣṭhira
english: On this point too they relate an ancient tale, the dialogue of Kapila and the Cow. Mark it well, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: āmnāyam anupaśyan hi purāṇaṃ śāśvataṃ dhruvam nahuṣaḥ pūrvam ālebhe tvaṣṭur gām iti naḥ śrutam
english: Beholding the ancient, eternal, abiding tradition, Nahuṣa long ago took a cow belonging to Tvaṣṭṛ — so we have heard.

sanskrit: tāṃ niyuktām adīnātmā sattvasthaḥ samaye rataḥ jñānavān niyatāhāro dadarśa kapilas tadā
english: That cow, made ready for sacrifice, the sage Kapila then beheld — he of undejected spirit, steadfast in goodness, delighting in righteous custom, possessed of knowledge, restrained in his eating.

sanskrit: sa buddhim uttamāṃ prāpto naiṣṭhikīm akutobhayām smarāmi śithilaṃ satyaṃ vedā ity abravīt sakṛt
english: Having attained the highest understanding, perfected and fearless from every side, he said but once: "I recall it but faintly — the truth is loose-held: 'the Vedas,' indeed!"

sanskrit: tāṃ gām ṛṣiḥ syūmaraśmiḥ praviśya yatim abravīt haṃho vedā yadi matā dharmāḥ kenāpare matāḥ
english: Then the seer Syūmaraśmi, entering into that cow, spoke to the ascetic: "Ho there! If the Vedas are held to be authoritative, by what are other duties to be held authoritative?"

sanskrit: tapasvino dhṛtimataḥ śrutivijñānacakṣuṣaḥ sarvam ārṣaṃ hi manyante vyāhṛtaṃ viditātmanaḥ
english: For of the ascetic, the resolute, who has the eye of scriptural discernment and has come to know the Self, men hold that all his utterance is of the seers.

sanskrit: tasyaivaṃ gatatṛṣṇasya vijvarasya nirāśiṣaḥ kā vivakṣāsti vedeṣu nirārambhasya sarvaśaḥ
english: For one whose craving has thus departed, who is freed of fever and of every longing, undertaking nothing at all — what desire to expound the Vedas can remain to him?

sanskrit: kapila uvāca nāhaṃ vedān vinindāmi na vivakṣāmi karhi cit pṛthag āśramiṇāṃ karmāṇy ekārthānīti naḥ śrutam
english: Kapila said: I do not revile the Vedas, nor do I ever wish to dispute them. We have heard that the works of those in the several stages of life, though distinct, have one and the same aim.

sanskrit: gacchaty eva parityāgī vānaprasthaś ca gacchati gṛhastho brahmacārī ca ubhau tāv api gacchataḥ
english: The renouncer surely reaches the goal, and the forest-dweller reaches it; the householder and the celibate student — both of these too reach it.

sanskrit: devayānā hi panthānaś catvāraḥ śāśvatā matāḥ teṣāṃ jyāyaḥkanīyastvaṃ phaleṣūktaṃ balābalam
english: Four are the eternal paths held to lead toward the gods; among them their greater and lesser standing, their strength and weakness, is told in terms of their fruits.

sanskrit: evaṃ viditvā sarvārthān ārabhed iti vaidikam nārabhed iti cānyatra naiṣṭhikī śrūyate śrutiḥ
english: Having thus understood all these aims, "let him undertake works" — so runs the Vedic injunction; and elsewhere "let him not undertake them" — so is heard the scripture of final renunciation.

sanskrit: anārambhe hy adoṣaḥ syād ārambhe 'doṣa uttamaḥ evaṃ sthitasya śāstrasya durvijñeyaṃ balābalam
english: In non-action there may be freedom from fault; in action there is the highest faultlessness. Of scripture standing thus, the relative strength is hard indeed to discern.

sanskrit: yady atra kiṃ cit pratyakṣam ahiṃsāyāḥ paraṃ matam ṛte tv āgamaśāstrebhyo brūhi tad yadi paśyasi
english: If there is here anything immediately evident, held higher than non-injury yet apart from the scriptures of tradition — declare it, if you can see it.

sanskrit: syūmaraśmir uvāca svargakāmo yajeteti satataṃ śrūyate śrutiḥ phalaṃ prakalpya pūrvaṃ hi tato yajñaḥ pratāyate
english: Syūmaraśmi said: "Let him who desires heaven offer sacrifice" — so the scripture is ever heard. For first the fruit is set forth, and only thereupon is the sacrifice extended.

sanskrit: ajaś cāśvaś ca meṣaś ca gauś ca pakṣigaṇāś ca ye grāmyāraṇyā oṣadhayaḥ prāṇasyānnam iti śrutiḥ
english: The goat and the horse and the ram, the cow, and the flocks of birds, and the plants of village and of wilderness — "all these are the food of life" — so says the scripture.

sanskrit: tathaivānnaṃ hy aharahaḥ sāyaṃ prātar nirupyate paśavaś cātha dhānyaṃ ca yajñasyāṅgam iti śrutiḥ
english: Just so is food day by day apportioned, at evening and at dawn; and the cattle and the grain are members of the sacrifice — so says the scripture.

sanskrit: etāni saha yajñena prajāpatir akalpayat tena prajāpatir devān yajñenāyajata prabhuḥ
english: These together with the sacrifice did Prajāpati ordain; and with that sacrifice the Lord Prajāpati worshipped the gods.

sanskrit: te smānyonyaṃcarāḥ sarve prāṇinaḥ sapta sapta ca yajñeṣūpākṛtaṃ viśvaṃ prāhur uttamasaṃjñitam
english: All these living beings, moving each upon the other, are sevenfold and sevenfold; and the whole world, brought to bear within sacrifices, men call the thing named Highest.

sanskrit: etac caivābhyanujñātaṃ pūrvaiḥ pūrvatarais tathā ko jātu na vicinvīta vidvān svāṃ śaktim ātmanaḥ
english: This too was sanctioned by the ancients and by those still more ancient. What wise man would ever fail to weigh well his own capacity?

sanskrit: paśavaś ca manuṣyāś ca drumāś cauṣadhibhiḥ saha svargam evābhikāṅkṣante na ca svargas tv ṛte makham
english: Beasts and men and trees together with the plants all long for heaven alone; yet heaven there is none apart from sacrifice.

sanskrit: oṣadhyaḥ paśavo vṛkṣā vīrud ājyaṃ payo dadhi havir bhūmir diśaḥ śraddhā kālaś caitāni dvādaśa
english: Plants, cattle, trees, creeper, clarified butter, milk, curds, oblation, earth, the quarters, faith, and time — these are the twelve.

sanskrit: ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni yajamānaś ca ṣoḍaśaḥ agnir jñeyo gṛhapatiḥ sa saptadaśa ucyate aṅgāny etāni yajñasya yajño mūlam iti śrutiḥ
english: The Ṛc verses, the Yajus, the Sāman, and the sacrificer as the sixteenth; the fire is to be known as the householder, and that is called the seventeenth. These are the members of the sacrifice, and the sacrifice is the root — so says the scripture.

sanskrit: ājyena payasā dadhnā śakṛtāmikṣayā tvacā vālaiḥ śṛṅgeṇa pādena saṃbhavaty eva gaur makham evaṃ pratyekaśaḥ sarvaṃ yad yad asya vidhīyate
english: With its clarified butter, its milk, its curds, its dung, its curd-and-milk mixture, its hide, its hairs, its horn, its hoof — the cow becomes the very sacrifice; thus each single part of it serves whatever purpose is ordained for it.

sanskrit: yajñaṃ vahanti saṃbhūya sahartvigbhiḥ sadakṣiṇaiḥ saṃhatyaitāni sarvāṇi yajñaṃ nirvartayanty uta
english: Joined together with the priests and with the sacrificial fees, they bear the sacrifice onward; and all these things, brought together, bring the sacrifice to its completion.

sanskrit: yajñārthāni hi sṛṣṭāni yathā vai śrūyate śrutiḥ evaṃ pūrve pūrvatarāḥ pravṛttāś caiva mānavāḥ
english: For they were created for the sake of sacrifice, even as the scripture is heard to declare; and thus the ancients and the still more ancient among men engaged in works.

sanskrit: na hinasti hy ārabhate nābhidruhyati kiṃ cana yajño yaṣṭavya ity eva yo yajaty aphalepsayā
english: He does no harm, though he acts; he bears malice toward nothing — he who sacrifices thinking only "the sacrifice is to be offered," with no craving for its fruit.

sanskrit: yajñāṅgāny api caitāni yathoktāni nasaṃśayaḥ vidhinā vidhiyuktāni tārayanti parasparam
english: And these members of the sacrifice, as has been told, beyond doubt, when joined to one another by the prescribed rule, carry one another across.

sanskrit: āmnāyam ārṣaṃ paśyāmi yasmin vedāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ taṃ vidvāṃso 'nupaśyanti brāhmaṇasyānudarśanāt
english: I behold the tradition of the seers, in which the Vedas are established; the wise perceive it through their contemplation of the Brahman.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaprabhavo yajño brāhmaṇārpaṇa eva ca anu yajñaṃ jagat sarvaṃ yajñaś cānu jagat sadā
english: The sacrifice springs from the Brahman and is offered up into the Brahman; the whole world follows after the sacrifice, and the sacrifice ever follows after the world.

sanskrit: om iti brahmaṇo yonir namaḥ svāhā svadhā vaṣaṭ yasyaitāni prayujyante yathāśakti kṛtāny api
english: "Om" is the womb of the Brahman; "Namaḥ," "Svāhā," "Svadhā," "Vaṣaṭ" — he by whom these are employed, performed according to his power, however slight —

sanskrit: na tasya triṣu lokeṣu paralokabhayaṃ viduḥ iti vedā vadantīha siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ
english: of him they know no fear of the world beyond, throughout the three worlds — so the Vedas declare here, and the perfected ones and the supreme seers.

sanskrit: ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni stobhāś ca vidhicoditāḥ yasminn etāni sarvāṇi bahir eva sa vai dvijaḥ
english: The Ṛc verses, the Yajus, the Sāman, and the chant-syllables impelled by the rule — he in whom all these dwell outwardly, he indeed is the twice-born.

sanskrit: agnyādheye yad bhavati yac ca some sute dvija yac cetarair mahāyajñair veda tad bhagavān svataḥ
english: What comes to be in the kindling of the sacred fire, and in the pressed Soma, twice-born one, and what comes by the other great sacrifices — all that the venerable one knows of his own self.

sanskrit: tasmād brahman yajetaiva yājayec cāvicārayan yajataḥ svargavidhinā pretya svargaphalaṃ mahat
english: Therefore, brahmin, let him surely sacrifice and cause sacrifice to be made, without hesitation; for one who sacrifices by the rite that wins heaven, the fruit of heaven hereafter is great.

sanskrit: nāyaṃ loko 'sty ayajñānāṃ paraś ceti viniścayaḥ vedavādavidaś caiva pramāṇam ubhayaṃ tadā
english: For those who do not sacrifice there is neither this world nor the next — so is the settled judgement; and those versed in the doctrine of the Veda are then the authority for both.

sanskrit: kapila uvāca etāvad anupaśyanto yatayo yānti mārgagāḥ naiṣāṃ sarveṣu lokeṣu kaś cid asti vyatikramaḥ
english: Kapila said: Beholding only thus much, the ascetics go forward as travellers of the path; for them, throughout all the worlds, there is no transgression at all.

sanskrit: nirdvaṃdvā nirnamaskārā nirāśīrbandhanā budhāḥ vimuktāḥ sarvapāpebhyaś caranti śucayo 'malāḥ
english: Beyond the pairs of opposites, free of homage, unbound by any longing, the wise ones, released from all sins, wander pure and stainless.

sanskrit: apavarge 'tha saṃtyāge buddhau ca kṛtaniścayāḥ brahmiṣṭhā brahmabhūtāś ca brahmaṇy eva kṛtālayāḥ
english: Resolved upon final release, upon renunciation, and upon true understanding, most devoted to the Brahman, having become the Brahman, they have made their dwelling in the Brahman alone.

sanskrit: viśokā naṣṭarajasas teṣāṃ lokāḥ sanātanāḥ teṣāṃ gatiṃ parāṃ prāpya gārhasthye kiṃ prayojanam
english: Free of grief, with passion destroyed, theirs are the everlasting worlds. When one has attained their supreme goal, what need has he of the householder's life?

sanskrit: syūmaraśmir uvāca yady eṣā paramā niṣṭhā yady eṣā paramā gatiḥ gṛhasthān avyapāśritya nāśramo 'nyaḥ pravartate
english: Syūmaraśmi said: Even if this be the highest consummation, even if this be the supreme goal, no other stage of life can proceed without depending upon the householders.

sanskrit: yathā mātaram āśritya sarve jīvanti jantavaḥ evaṃ gṛhastham āśritya vartanta itare ''śramāḥ
english: As all creatures live by depending upon their mother, so the other stages of life subsist by depending upon the householder.

sanskrit: gṛhastha eva yajate gṛhasthas tapyate tapaḥ gārhasthyam asya dharmasya mūlaṃ yat kiṃ cid ejate
english: It is the householder who sacrifices, the householder who practises austerity; the householder's estate is the root of this whole order of duty, of whatever stirs and lives.

sanskrit: prajanād dhy abhinirvṛttāḥ sarve prāṇabhṛto mune prajanaṃ cāpy utānyatra na kathaṃ cana vidyate
english: For all bearers of breath, O sage, are brought forth through procreation; and procreation, moreover, is in no wise to be found elsewhere.

sanskrit: yās tāḥ syur bahir oṣadhyo bahv araṇyās tathā dvija oṣadhibhyo bahir yasmāt prāṇī kaś cin na vidyate kasyaiṣā vāg bhavet satyā mokṣo nāsti gṛhād iti
english: Whatever plants there be without, and the many of the wilderness too, O twice-born — since beyond the plants no living being is to be found, for whom could this saying hold true, that "there is no release outside the household"?

sanskrit: aśraddadhānair aprājñaiḥ sūkṣmadarśanavarjitaiḥ nirāśair alasaiḥ śrāntais tapyamānaiḥ svakarmabhiḥ śramasyoparamo dṛṣṭaḥ pravrajyā nāma paṇḍitaiḥ
english: By the faithless, the unwise, bereft of subtle insight, the despairing, the slothful, the weary, tormented by their own works, the cessation of toil — that which is called renunciation — has been devised, while passing for learned men.

sanskrit: trailokyasyaiva hetur hi maryādā śāśvatī dhruvā brāhmaṇo nāma bhagavāñ janmaprabhṛti pūjyate
english: For the very cause of the three worlds is the eternal, abiding bound of order; and he who is named the brahmin, the venerable one, is honoured from his birth onward.

sanskrit: prāg garbhādhānān mantrā hi pravartante dvijātiṣu aviśrambheṣu vartante viśrambheṣv apy asaṃśayam
english: For among the twice-born the sacred formulas begin even before the implanting of the embryo; they attend, beyond doubt, both upon the unconfiding rites and upon the confiding ones.

sanskrit: dāhaḥ punaḥ saṃśrayaṇe saṃsthite pātrabhojanam dānaṃ gavāṃ paśūnāṃ vā piṇḍānāṃ cāpsu majjanam
english: And again the cremation upon his death, the eating from the vessel when he is laid out, the gift of cows or of cattle, and the sinking of the rice-balls in the waters —

sanskrit: arciṣmanto barhiṣadaḥ kravyādāḥ pitaraḥ smṛtāḥ mṛtasyāpy anumanyante mantrā mantrāś ca kāraṇam
english: The fathers, the flame-possessing, the seated-on-sacred-grass, the eaters of the offerings, are remembered in the rites; the sacred formulas give their sanction even to the dead, and the formulas are the cause.

sanskrit: evaṃ krośatsu vedeṣu kuto mokṣo 'sti kasya cit ṛṇavanto yadā martyāḥ pitṛdevadvijātiṣu
english: While the Vedas thus cry aloud, whence is there release for anyone, since mortals stand in debt to the fathers, the gods, and the twice-born?

sanskrit: śriyā vihīnair alasaiḥ paṇḍitair apalāpitam vedavādāparijñānaṃ satyābhāsam ivānṛtam
english: It is by men bereft of glory, slothful, calling themselves learned, that the ignorance of the Veda's doctrine is talked away as though it were knowledge — falsehood wearing the semblance of truth.

sanskrit: na vai pāpair hriyate kṛṣyate vā; yo brāhmaṇo yajate vedaśāstraiḥ ūrdhvaṃ yajñaḥ paśubhiḥ sārdham eti; saṃtarpitas tarpayate ca kāmaiḥ
english: He is not carried off by sins nor dragged down — the brahmin who sacrifices according to the Veda's ordinances; his sacrifice goes upward together with the beasts, and, being sated, it sates him with the objects of desire.

sanskrit: na vedānāṃ paribhavān na śāṭhyena na māyayā mahat prāpnoti puruṣo brahma brahmaṇi vindati
english: Not by contempt of the Vedas, not by guile, not by deceit, does a man attain the great; he finds the Brahman within the Brahman.

sanskrit: kapila uvāca darśaṃ ca paurṇamāsaṃ ca agnihotraṃ ca dhīmatām cāturmāsyāni caivāsaṃs teṣu yajñaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Kapila said: The new-moon and the full-moon rites, the fire-oblation of the wise, and the four-monthly observances — in these abode the everlasting sacrifice.

sanskrit: anārambhāḥ sudhṛtayaḥ śucayo brahmasaṃśritāḥ brahmaṇaiva sma te devāṃs tarpayanty amṛtaiṣiṇaḥ
english: Undertaking no works, well-steadied, pure, given over to the Brahman, those seekers after the immortal sate the gods by the Brahman alone.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtātmabhūtasya sarvabhūtāni paśyataḥ devāpi mārge muhyanti apadasya padaiṣiṇaḥ
english: For him who has become the Self of all beings, who beholds all beings, who is without a track yet seeks the track — upon his road even the gods grow bewildered.

sanskrit: caturdvāraṃ puruṣaṃ caturmukhaṃ; caturdhā cainam upayāti nindā bāhubhyāṃ vāca udarād upasthāt; teṣāṃ dvāraṃ dvārapālo bubhūṣet
english: The man is a city of four gates, four-faced; and fourfold does blame come upon him — from his two arms, from his speech, from his belly, from his loins. Of these gates one should wish to be the gatekeeper.

sanskrit: nākṣair dīvyen nādadītānyavittaṃ; na vāyonīyasya śṛtaṃ pragṛhṇet kruddho na caiva prahareta dhīmāṃs; tathāsya tat pāṇipādaṃ suguptam
english: Let him not gamble with the dice, nor take another's wealth, nor receive the cooked food of a man of unworthy birth; and the wise one, when angered, should never strike — thus are his hand and foot well guarded.

sanskrit: nākrośam archen na mṛṣā vadec ca; na paiśunaṃ janavādaṃ ca kuryāt satyavrato mitabhāṣo 'pramattas; tathāsya vāgdvāram atho suguptam
english: Let him not give way to reviling, nor speak falsely, nor practise slander or idle gossip among men; vowed to truth, sparing of speech, ever heedful — thus is the gate of his speech well guarded.

sanskrit: nānāśanaḥ syān na mahāśanaḥ syād; alolupaḥ sādhubhir āgataḥ syāt yātrārtham āhāram ihādadīta; tathāsya syāj jāṭharī dvāraguptiḥ
english: Let him not be a glutton, nor a great eater; let him be free of greed, and take his food as brought to him by the good; let him receive here only such food as serves to sustain his journey — thus is his belly's gate kept guarded.

sanskrit: na vīrapatnīṃ vihareta nārīṃ; na cāpi nārīm anṛtāv āhvayīta bhāryāvrataṃ hy ātmani dhārayīta; tathāsyopasthadvāraguptir bhaveta
english: Let him not dally with a woman who is a hero's wife, nor summon a woman to him out of season; let him hold to himself the vow of fidelity to his wife — thus would the guarding of his loins' gate be kept.

sanskrit: dvārāṇi yasya sarvāṇi suguptāni manīṣiṇaḥ upastham udaraṃ bāhū vāk caturthī sa vai dvijaḥ
english: The wise man whose gates are all well guarded — the loins, the belly, the arms, and the speech as the fourth — he indeed is the twice-born.

sanskrit: moghāny aguptadvārasya sarvāṇy eva bhavanty uta kiṃ tasya tapasā kāryaṃ kiṃ yajñena kim ātmanā
english: For him whose gates are unguarded, all his deeds become vain; what use to him is austerity, what use the sacrifice, what use his very self?

sanskrit: anuttarīyavasanam anupastīrṇaśāyinam bāhūpadhānaṃ śāmyantaṃ taṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ
english: Him who wears no upper garment, who lies down on no spread couch, whose pillow is his own arm, who has grown still — him the gods know for a brahmin.

sanskrit: dvaṃdvārāmeṣu sarveṣu ya eko ramate muniḥ pareṣām ananudhyāyaṃs taṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ
english: The sage who, alone, takes delight amid all those who delight in the pairs of opposites, brooding upon no thoughts of others — him the gods know for a brahmin.

sanskrit: yena sarvam idaṃ buddhaṃ prakṛtir vikṛtiś ca yā gatijñaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ taṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ
english: He by whom all this is understood, both nature and its modification, who knows the course of all beings — him the gods know for a brahmin.

sanskrit: abhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyaḥ sarveṣām abhayaṃ yataḥ sarvabhūtātmabhūto yas taṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ
english: From whom there is safety for all beings, since from him all are without fear, who has become the Self of all beings — him the gods know for a brahmin.

sanskrit: nāntareṇānujānanti vedānāṃ yat kriyāphalam anujñāya ca tat sarvam anyad rocayate 'phalam
english: They do not deny the fruit of action that belongs to the Vedas as a thing apart; yet having granted all that, they find their pleasure in another thing that bears no fruit.

sanskrit: phalavanti ca karmāṇi vyuṣṭimanti dhruvāṇi ca viguṇāni ca paśyanti tathānaikāntikāni ca
english: And they see that works are fruitful, yielding their reward, and abiding; yet also that they are flawed and not unfailing in their issue.

sanskrit: guṇāś cātra sudurjñeyā jñātāś cāpi suduṣkarāḥ anuṣṭhitāś cāntavanta iti tvam anupaśyasi
english: And here the merits are most hard to know, and even when known, most hard to perform; and once performed, they have an end — so do you perceive.

sanskrit: syūmaraśmir uvāca yathā ca vedaprāmāṇyaṃ tyāgaś ca saphalo yathā tau panthānāv ubhau vyaktau bhagavaṃs tad bravīhi me
english: Syūmaraśmi said: How the authority of the Veda stands, and how renunciation bears its fruit, and how both these paths are made manifest — declare that to me, O venerable one.

sanskrit: kapila uvāca pratyakṣam iha paśyanti bhavantaḥ satpathe sthitāḥ pratyakṣaṃ tu kim atrāsti yad bhavanta upāsate
english: Kapila said: You who stand upon the true path behold here what is immediately evident; yet what is there here, immediately evident, that you reverently attend upon?

sanskrit: syūmaraśmir uvāca syūmaraśmir ahaṃ brahmañ jijñāsārtham ihāgataḥ śreyaskāmaḥ pratyavocam ārjavān na vivakṣayā imaṃ ca saṃśayaṃ ghoraṃ bhagavān prabravītu me
english: Syūmaraśmi said: I am Syūmaraśmi, brahmin, come here for the sake of knowledge; desiring the highest good, I have answered you out of sincerity and not out of any wish to dispute. Let the venerable one resolve for me this terrible doubt.

sanskrit: pratyakṣam iha paśyanto bhavantaḥ satpathe sthitāḥ kim atra pratyakṣatamaṃ bhavanto yad upāsate anyatra tarkaśāstrebhya āgamāc ca yathāgamam
english: You who stand upon the true path, beholding here what is immediately evident — what is here most evident of all, that you reverently attend upon, apart from the sciences of reasoning and from tradition followed each according to its tradition?

sanskrit: āgamo vedavādas tu tarkaśāstrāṇi cāgamaḥ yathāgamam upāsīta āgamas tatra sidhyati siddhiḥ pratyakṣarūpā ca dṛśyaty āgamaniścayāt
english: Tradition is the doctrine of the Veda, and the sciences of reasoning too are tradition; let one attend upon it each according to his tradition, and there tradition is made effective; and perfection in the form of the immediately evident is seen to arise from the certainty of tradition.

sanskrit: naur nāvīva nibaddhā hi srotasā sanibandhanā hriyamāṇā kathaṃ vipra kubuddhīṃs tārayiṣyati etad bravītu bhagavān upapanno 'smy adhīhi bhoḥ
english: As one boat bound fast to another, both swept along together by the current — how, O brahmin, shall it carry the dull-witted across? Let the venerable one declare this; I have come fittingly to you — teach me, sir.

sanskrit: naiva tyāgī na saṃtuṣṭo nāśoko na nirāmayaḥ na nirvivitso nāvṛtto nāpavṛtto 'sti kaś cana
english: There is none who is truly a renouncer, none truly content, none free of grief, none free of ill, none free of curiosity, none turned away, none turned wholly back.

sanskrit: bhavanto 'pi ca hṛṣyanti śocanti ca yathā vayam indriyārthāś ca bhavatāṃ samānāḥ sarvajantuṣu
english: You too rejoice and grieve, even as we do; and the objects of your senses are the same as those of all living creatures.
